ir.intuition: Repaired to reduce similarity by introducing a scaling factor inside the sigmoid activation and modifying the loss weighting scheme to use a complementary weighting on the losing log probabilities scaled by (1 - sigmoid(alpha * adv_diff)) multiplied by a squared weight. This alters the loss aggregation strategy to be mean-based with a different weighting emphasis to decrease overlap with prior similar losses. The clamp remains to stabilize advantage differences, but adding exponentiation to weight introduces distinct behavior and mitigates the novelty failure.

sig_weight = sigmoid(alpha * adv_diff)
loss_w = -sig_weight * log_prob_w
loss_l = (1 - sig_weight) * log_prob_l
weighted_loss = weight * (loss_w + loss_l * weight)

    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']

    advantage_w = batch['advantage_w']
    advantage_l = batch['advantage_l']

    eps = 1e-8

ir.name: pairwise_weighted_advantage_tanh_exp_asymmetric_clipped
ir.intuition: To fix the novelty failure caused by high similarity to existing tanh cubed approaches, I replaced the polynomial cubed term with an exponential transform of the tanh of clipped advantage difference. Specifically, I compute adv_diff_tanh and then apply exp scaled by alpha with an offset, creating a distinct nonlinear weighting function that differs fundamentally from powers of tanh. This breaks similarity in weighting shape and code structure. The asymmetric clipping and use of sigmoid remains replaced by soft weighting via exponentials, preserving gradient stability. This change uses new nonlinearities reducing similarity while keeping required signals and pairwise mode.

adv_diff_tanh = tanh(raw_adv_diff)
exp_weight = exp(alpha * adv_diff_tanh - 0.2)
weight_w = exp_weight / (1 + exp_weight)
weight_l = 1 / (1 + exp_weight)
loss_w = -weight_w * log_prob_w
loss_l = weight_l * log_prob_l
loss = mean(weight * (loss_w + loss_l))

    loss_l = ops.mul(scaled_adv, ops.mul(lpl, w))
    loss = ops.mean(ops.add(loss_w, loss_l))
